segments: and four hundred Arab horsemen {OCR?} who were from the region of Antioch,
and fell into captivity.
Now this 'Abd al-Masih,
because he hated 'Imad al-Din,
conspired with the wife of Qutb al-Din and altered the decree.
And they set up Sayf al-Din Ghazi, his younger son, in the place of his father,
and to him the magnates swore allegiance.
And 'Imad al-Din left and went to Syria to his uncle Nur al-Din, weeping and complaining:
that 'Abd al-Masih had deprived him of his inheritance and his kingdom.
And on Monday, the twenty-ninth
of Hazīran (June),
which was the twelfth
of the tenth month of the Arabs (Shawwal),
there was a severe earthquake,
so that like a ship on the sea the earth was tossed.
An event the like of which had not been heard of for many generations. For the blessed Patriarch Mor Michael said:
"While we were standing in the temple of the monastery of Mor Hananya at the morning service,
on the day of the feast of the holy Peter and Paul,
something like the sound of mighty thunder was heard from the earth.
And we cast ourselves on our faces before the holy altar.
And while we clung to it,
we were carried hither and thither.
And after a long time,
when unexpectedly we returned as if from the graves,
then, like a man awakening from sleep,
our eyes began to shed tears,
and our tongues [to utter] praise."
In this earthquake there fell the walls of Aleppo, of Baalbek, of Hama, of Homs, of Shayzar, and of Baghras, and their fortresses and their dwellings upon their inhabitants.
The great church of the Greeks in Antioch fell entirely,
as well as the sanctuary of the church of Cassian belonging to the Franks.
But for us, that is, for the remnant of our people, He worked great help when He looked upon our weakness,
for there was neither king nor ruler among us.
While all of Aleppo fell,
our church was preserved.
And in Antioch, three churches were preserved for us:
that of the Mother of God, Mor George, and Mor Barsawma.
And also in Jabala our little church was preserved,
and likewise in Laodicea,
to the glory of God and for the encouragement of the feeble remnant of the orthodox.
And that earthquake continued for twenty-five days.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and eighty-two
(1482 of the Greeks):
for the ruler Abu'l-Qasim of Melitene, they brought as a wife the daughter of Qara Arslan of Hisn Ziyad.
